description: The bar chart illustrates the Shapley value for different models across various categories. The horizontal axis displays the categories labeled L_4⁺, L₃, L₂, L₁, T, R₁, R₂, R₃, and R₄⁺, arranged in that specific order. The vertical axis represents the ‘Shapley value’ on a linear scale ranging from 0 to 80, with tick marks at intervals of 20.  For each category, there is a group of three bars representing the models mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and chLSTM (green). Within the category T, the mBERT bar reaches approximately 50, the XLM-R bar is around 70, and the chLSTM bar extends to the maximum value of 80. In contrast, the bars for categories L_4⁺, L₃, L₂, L₁, R₂, R₃, and R₄⁺ are generally below a value of 15 for all three models. The R₁ bars consistently show higher values than the corresponding L₁ bars across all models; for example, XLM-R has a value of approximately 10 for L₁ and 14 for R₁. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or outlining.
caption_used: The bar chart illustrates the Shapley value for different models across various categories. The horizontal axis represents the categories labeled as L_4^+, L_3, L_2, L_1, T, R_1, R_2, R_3, R_4^+, while the vertical axis represents the 'Shapley value,' measured on a linear scale from 0 to 80 with tick intervals of 20 units. Bars are grouped by category, with each group containing three bars representing different models: mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and chLSTM (green). The tallest bars appear in category T, where mBERT has an approximate value of 50, XLM-R about 70, and chLSTM reaching the maximum value of 80. In other categories such as L_4^+, L_3, L_2, L_1, R_1, R_2, R_3, and R_4^+, the bars are all relatively short, generally below 15. Notably, the values for R_1 consistently exceed those for L_1 across all models, indicating a stronger contribution from the right context. A legend is provided in the top right corner.
